extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: RoboBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs. It includes datasets across diverse embodiments, attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation, and introduces an MLLM-as-world-simulator evaluation framework for planning.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang (Peking University, Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, Fudan University, University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data is collected from open-source large-scale real robotic datasets and in-house collection. Each dimension has a customized data workflow involving preprocessing, annotation with VLMs, detection models or human experts, and Q&A format generation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Large-scale real-world robotic datasets including RH20T, Open X-Embodiment, RDT-1B, RoboMIND, AgiBot World, and other high-quality robotic videos; also in-house collected data.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data filtering during construction and post-construction validation. General criteria address image quality and task validity, while sub-benchmarks have tailored rules—such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks. A majority-vote strategy is applied: items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are generated using a combination of VLMs (Gemini), detection models, and human experts. For planning, Gemini generates structured annotations—task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata—which are refined by human annotators. For perception, human-labeled bounding boxes and manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes are used. Execution-level failures are labeled by experts. Implicit instructions are generated by rewriting explicit ones using LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A majority-vote strategy is used: items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction. Additionally, 20 professionally trained annotators conduct comprehensive quality inspections, validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (for video segmentation, structured annotation generation, and functional attribute QA generation); GPT (for generating functional properties and distractors for object-centric data)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left–right arm assignments or positional movements, limiting cross-embodiment planning. Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions due to lack of real-world planning failure data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation/benchmarking of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation, covering instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis.

name.evidence: We introduce RoboBench, a benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains.

description.evidence: RoboBench defines five dimensions—Instruction Comprehension, Perception Reasoning, Generalized Planning, Affordance Prediction, and Failure Analysis—that together capture the interdependent capabilities required for embodied cognition... spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs.

inLanguage.evidence: RoboBench defines five dimensions—Instruction Comprehension, Perception Reasoning, Generalized Planning, Affordance Prediction, and Failure Analysis

rai:dataCollection.evidence: To evaluate the five cognitive dimensions, we build datasets from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations, aligning each sub-benchmark with the embodied task pipeline for realism.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Data combine large-scale real-world robotic datasets Fang et al. (2023); Collaboration et al. (2023); Liu et al. (2024c); Wu et al. (2024); Bu et al. (2025) with curated in-house collection, narrowing the sim-to-real gap.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We build a planning pool from high-quality robotic videos Collaboration et al. (2023); Lin et al. (2024a); Liu et al. (2024b;c); Fang et al. (2023); Wu et al. (2024); Mu et al. (2023); Yang et al. (2024), extracting frame sequences as standardized inputs.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We adopt a two-stage quality control process to ensure benchmark quality: data filtering during construction and post-construction validation. In the construction stage, We apply both general and task-specific filters. General criteria address image quality and task validity, while sub-benchmarks have tailored rules—such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks... We further adopt a majority-vote strategy: items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Gemini Comanici et al. (2025) generates structured annotations—task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata (objects, actions, scenes, embodiments)—which are refined by human annotators... scene-centric, leveraging Gemini-segmented video steps for temporal grounding, together with manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes for spatial and causal reasoning; and task-centric, with human-labeled bounding boxes linking long-horizon instructions to target objects.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We recruite 20 professionally trained annotators to conduct comprehensive quality inspections, validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. We further adopt a majority-vote strategy: items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Gemini Comanici et al. rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We attribute this to the nature of existing planning data, which primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left–right arm assignments or positional movements... planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order) due to lack of real-world planning failure data.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We introduce RoboBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating MLLMs as embodied brains across 5 key dimensions, spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs... RoboBench provides a comprehensive scaffold to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence.
